note:
Swap all three Key Findings images on /pages/matrixyl-3000-research. Generated by the wave `block-matrixyl-research-medical` (brief at configs/banners/block-matrixyl-research-medical.json, commit a79f93f) - 31 candidates across 6 suppliers, 3 slots.

MALCOLM'S PICK, 2026-08-25: the nbp_flash_01 SET, all three blocks from one engine and one candidate index. He chose the set, not three separate winners, and that is the point - the three sit stacked on one page and the object language has to be identical. nbp_flash_01 gives the same hard-surface glossy CGI, the same translucent glass base under the specimen, the same pale high-key ground, across all three.

WHAT WAS OFFERED AND NOT TAKEN: gpt_image_02 read stronger on mechanism in f1 (a more obvious sparse-to-dense gradient in the fibre network) but is a softer, more painterly render that sits differently against nbp_flash's crisp CGI. Set coherence won. Not a defect in the rejected set - a different call.

MECHANISM PER BLOCK, unchanged from the brief - the three must not be interchangeable:
  f1  Robinson 2005, split-face RCT, 93 women, 12 weeks, measured improvement in the appearance of lines. ONE continuous furrow, deeper at the near end, shallower where the teal network beneath has been reinforced. NO split-face frame: a split asserts a result by juxtaposition and these engines render it as a hard seam.
  f2  Sederma in-vitro, +117% Collagen I / +327% Collagen IV in CULTURED cells. An isolated specimen on a translucent base - not a body - with spindle cells lit and extruding new fibre, and a dense flat mat along the bottom.
  f3  Katayama 1993, the peptide SIGNALS cells to build. The docking event itself: chains seated in the membrane, a pulse converging on the cell's centre, new fibre streaming from both arms.

THE ACTIVE IS A PEPTIDE CHAIN, NOT COPPER BEADS. Matrixyl 3000 has no metal in it - it is a tripeptide and a tetrapeptide - so each sphere holds a short chain of linked beads in two lengths, three and four. Copper and gold were negated by name so this set can never blur with the copper-peptide page's Clinical blue.

COLOUR: Teal 016569 per the concern-to-colour map. Tissue stays the r3 desaturated peach-cream - anatomy, not a brand colour.

JUDGED AT RENDER SIZE, NOT ONLY AT NATIVE. Live box is 1:1 at every width - 350x350 mobile, 660x660 desktop, capped at 720 by sizes='(max-width: 999px) 100vw, min(720px, 50vw)', object-fit cover. A square master is delivered whole and nothing crops (measured on the sister page, page-copper-peptide-research-key-finding-3.json). All three were checked at 660 and 350 before publishing.

SOURCE FORMAT. These masters are 4096x4096 PNG, which is ABOVE upload-theme-images.py's WEB_MAX_EDGE of 3000 - so optimise() takes its resize branch and does the JPEG encode itself (3000px, q95, 4:4:4, progressive, metadata stripped). No pre-conversion here, unlike the copper-peptide f3 job: that master was 2048px with no metadata and hit the early-return branch, which would have shipped PNG bytes under a .jpg filename. The rule is: below 3000px pre-convert explicitly, at or above 3000px let the script do it.

FILENAMES DO NOT PREFIX ONE ANOTHER. The uploader polls Shopify with `filename:<stem>*` and binds the first READY match, so a stem that prefixes a sibling stem can bind the wrong picture (this happened on 2026-08-24 with the glutathione serum). The three stems here share `skingenetix-matrixyl-3000-peptide-` and then diverge; none is a prefix of another. The `3000` will trip check_seo_name's digit warning - it is a real ingredient name with search value, and the warning is advisory.

WHAT IT REPLACES: three borrowed frames that have nothing to do with these findings - a product shot of the serum on f1, and the two /pages/our-philosophy pictures on f2 and f3. Per shopify.md rule 7 none of those files is touched, renamed or re-uploaded: Langify keys translations off the image URL. Only this page's references change; the originals stay live wherever else they are used.
